Dear Freedom of Information Officer,

I am writing to request information under the Freedom of Information Act 2000.

The South Wales Echo of 18 March 1983 reported a warehouse fire that destroyed archaeological finds held by the Glamorgan-Gwent Archaeological Trust. I understand the fire was in the area then covered by the West Glamorgan fire service (reported as Swansea; one later account gives Neath), and that the Service, formed in April 1996 from the earlier Dyfed, Powys and West Glamorgan brigades, may now hold some of that area's records. I am trying to establish whether material from earlier excavations at Llandough-juxta-Penarth, including the site of Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr / Cydfin Farm, was among the finds affected.

Please provide:

1. any incident record, fire report or fire investigation report held for a fire at premises used by the Glamorgan-Gwent Archaeological Trust in or around March 1983, showing the date and time, the address, the cause recorded and the extent of the damage;

2. if no such record is now held, the retention or disposal schedule under which West Glamorgan fire service incident records of 1983 were kept or destroyed, any record of their destruction, and whether any of those records were transferred to an archive (and, if so, which).

Personal data of third parties may be redacted. I am happy to receive the information by email.

I would welcome a short acknowledgement.

Kind regards,

Requester 
Royal Signals Cyber/ Electronic Warfare Professional

2. any earlier record of the building.

If such records exist, I would be grateful for a reference and a short description, and to know whether they are held by the Society or have been deposited with an archive.

I would welcome a short acknowledgement.

Dear HER Team,

Thank you for your three replies of 2 November 2026: on "Great House Farm, Llandough, Cardiff", on my request about the Llandough Roman villa and medieval house finds and the 1983 fire, and on my nomenclature supplement.

I would be grateful if Heneb would reconsider those answers, for these reasons.

1. Search, not research. I am not asking Heneb to research or interpret anything. I am asking whether the Historic Environment Record you maintain holds entries, files or correspondence under the names, grid references and dates I listed, and what searches were made to establish that. Searching your own record for named entries is part of answering a request, not research on my behalf.

2. The regime. The HER is kept on behalf of the Welsh Ministers under sections 194 and 195 of the Historic Environment (Wales) Act 2023. Information about cultural sites and built structures is environmental information under regulation 2(1)(f) of the Environmental Information Regulations 2004, and information held by another body on behalf of a public authority is held by that authority (regulation 3(2)(b)). I therefore ask that my requests be reconsidered as they would be under regulation 11 of the Regulations. If Heneb's view is that the Regulations do not apply to the HER, please tell me so and on what basis, so that I can put the same requests to the Welsh Ministers.

3. The searches made. For the 1983 fire and Roman villa request, please confirm whether the search covered the paper HER files and the GGAT archive for 1983 to 1989 and the names in my supplement, or the online Archwilio database only.

I would be grateful for your answer within 40 working days, as regulation 11(4) provides.


Kind regards,

Requester

Dear Requester,

ATISN 26-0075 - Great House Farm, Llandough

Thank you for your request which was received on 19 October.  You asked for:

A. ATISN 26-0010 – you request an internal review of the response provided on 19 October.

Please note that this is currently being conducted by the Welsh Government Departmental Records Officer under ref.  ATISN 26-0010 and will be responded to separately in due course.

B. ATISN 27589 (Cadw; your ref qA2496208)

You note the letter of 19 October 2026 refusing ATISN 27589 under section 14(2). You ask for a response on three points:

1. Section 14(2) applies only to a request that is substantially similar to an earlier one. You ask which points of ATISN 27589 the Welsh Government considers ATISN 27021 already covered. Point 3 of ATISN 27589 asked for "Any transfer, destruction or disposal of those files, with the schedule used and the date." You state that ATISN 27021 did not ask for that.

2. The letter stated that no new information "has been generated or become available". You ask for confirmation that this means that no information is held on any point of ATISN 27589 beyond what was released under ATISN 27021, or instead whether we declined to search again.

3. The letter sets out the right to complain to the Information Commissioner but not the internal review procedure, although it refers to the internal review of ATISN 27021. You ask how, and by when, you can ask for an internal review of ATISN 27589. You state that you will not treat the time for asking as running until Welsh Government have confirmed this.

You note that the question in point 3 of ATISN 27589 is also being dealt with under ATISN 26-0009 and state that you are note therefore making any new request under this submission.

C. New requests under the Freedom of Information Act 2000 and the Environmental Information Regulations 2004

You the following new requests for information concerning Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough-juxta-Penarth, Vale of Glamorgan:

1. Registered files. The internal review of ATISN 27021 identified registered files (including A--CL172-06-017/1 Community of Llandough, CL172-10-001/1, A--CL172-10-002/1, A--CL172-10-001/1, and six files of potential interest). For each file you request the register entry or index record showing its title, opening and closing dates, and current status (retained, transferred, destroyed or not traced) and, where the entry says a file was destroyed or transferred, the date and the record of the destruction or transfer. You state you are not asking for the contents of these files.

2. Property and deeds records. The response to ATISN 26-0010 stated that records of Welsh Government property, deeds and leasing are retained until the property is sold or the lease ends. You ask us to confirm whether the Welsh Government or the Welsh Office has ever owned, leased, acquired or disposed of any interest in land at Great House Farm, Leckwith Road or village green VG41, Llandough, between 1950 and 1997, and provide any deed, lease or property file record of it. You ask us to state if no information is held.

3. Wartime farm records, 1936–1955. You ask to provide any recorded information held by the Welsh Government, including records inherited from the Welsh Office, about the farm in 1936–1955:
(a) any record of the Glamorgan War Agricultural Executive Committee, or its post-war successor, about the farm, including any possession, requisition or cultivation direction;
(b) any claim or payment under the Compensation (Defence) Act 1939;
(c) any record naming the occupier or owner of the farm in that period.
Your understanding is that the 1941–43 National Farm Survey is held at The National Archives (MAF 32), and are not therefore requesting this. You ask us to us to provide the references for any other record has been transferred to The National Archives.

4. Compulsory purchase and stopping-up orders, 1950–1995. You ask us to confirm whether the Secretary of State for Wales or the Welsh Office made or confirmed any compulsory purchase order, stopping-up order or diversion order affecting the land at Great House Farm between 1950 and 1995, and provide a copy of any such order and of the decision confirming it. ATISN 26-0010 searched under the farm name and two company names. You state that Orders of this kind are usually titled by road or place, and request that we  also search under "Leckwith Road, Llandough", "Llandough-juxta-Penarth" and "Church View Close". You ask us to provide the references if such records have been transferred to The National Archives.

D. Preservation of records

You request that the following are not destroyed or weeded while ATISN 26-0009, the review in Part A, the requests in Part C and any complaint to the Information Commissioner remain open and reference your emails of 28 September and 1 October 2026:

1. the index of physical registered files, and the registered files themselves, referred to in the internal review of ATISN 27021 (including A--CL172-06-017/1, CL172-10-001/1, A--CL172-10-002/1, A--CL172-10-001/1 and the six files of potential interest identified in that review);
2. any 1988 listing file for Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, or any part or remnant of it;
3. the originals of the two inspection photographs dated 29 July 1988 released under ATISN 27021, with any negatives, digital files, envelopes, captions or other information recorded with them;
4. any disposal or destruction logs, certificates or schedules of destruction covering Welsh Office or Cadw records for 1970–1997;
5. the retention schedules in force for those records in 1970–1997;
6. any transfer lists to The National Archives or a Place of Deposit for those records, including any selection records made under OSP 7.


You will receive a response to Parts B – D above by 16 November 2026.  If you have any queries about this request, please do not hesitate to contact me at the address below.  Please remember to quote the reference number above in any future correspondence.

The request you sent me contains personal information about you - for example, your name and address. Dear Information Commissioner's Office,

Further to my email earlier today asking for more time (same thread, internal review outcome attached), please treat this email as my formal complaint under section 50 of the Freedom of Information Act 2000 about Amgueddfa Cymru – Museum Wales's handling of my request FOI 2026-024.

An extension of time is still my preference, so that I can send a fuller complaint. If you cannot grant one, please rely on this email as my complaint, made within six weeks of the internal review outcome of 22 September 2026.

Request: on 27 July 2026 I asked for recorded information about a discovery at Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr), Llandough-juxta-Penarth, near Cardiff (Heneb HER GGAT02038s; RCAHMW NPRN 20182). A published local history account records that a soldier's remains and his horse were found beneath the dining-room floor, that the remains were reburied in the churchyard, and that the visor and lance were given to the National Museum of Wales. I asked for accession, donation or transfer records, accession numbers and provenance notes, catalogue entries and correspondence, records of the associated remains, and any discovery or excavation reports.

Response: on 25 August 2026, one working day after the 20-working-day limit, the Museum said under section 1(1)(a) that it held no information. It also said its searches had found records of "other archaeological discoveries recorded at Great House Farm (Ty Mawr), Llandough", and that it had treated those as outside the request without describing them.

Internal review: I asked for a review on 26 August 2026. My point was that the searches were framed too narrowly around a "medieval visor, lance, helmet or other item of armour", and that the original find may have been described differently (for example as Roman). The review, issued on 22 September 2026, upheld the "not held" answer. It also said that those other records would receive "a separate response". I have not identified a response in which the Museum disclosed or described the records it set aside.

Why I believe the "not held" answer and its scope are doubtful:
1. The Museum confirms it holds records of archaeological discoveries at the same farm, yet it judged them unrelated without telling me what they are, so I cannot test that judgement. Whether they relate to the reported discovery is the question I asked.
2. Nomenclature is a major cause of confusion for all parties, and I ask the Commissioner and the Museum to take it into account. The same property appears in records as Great House Farm, Great House, Greathouse, Tŷ Mawr, Ty Mawr Farm, Tymawr, Cydfin Farm and Llandough Home Farm (1881 census). The place appears as Llandough, Llandough-juxta-Penarth, Llandough near Penarth and Llandough near Cardiff, and it is easily confused with Llandow in the Vale of Glamorgan. The Museum's own records use further terms: "Church Farm / Llandough Church Farm" in the provenance of accession 63.24 (medieval ironwork found about 1858), and "Llandough Farm (opposite hospital)", which is a separate farmstead. A search under one name or a modern object term can miss a record catalogued under another. I ask that the searches be repeated across all of these names, and across the donor names, periods and object descriptions a nineteenth-century accession might carry.
3. The reply was late (25 August against a due date of 24 August).

I ask the Commissioner to decide:
(a) whether, on the balance of probabilities, the Museum holds information within the scope of my request, including the records it set aside as "other discoveries" at Great House Farm and any record linked to accession 63.24;
(b) whether its searches were adequate, and to ask it to explain the search terms, name variants, systems and date ranges it used;
(c) that the Museum breached section 10(1) by replying late; and
(d) that the Museum should issue a fresh response covering the records it set aside.

The research behind this complaint, including the full name-variation index, is published at https://bucklerfamily.estate, and all ongoing research will continue to be published there.

The internal review outcome is attached. I can supply the original request (27 July), the Museum's response (25 August) and my review request (26 August) on request.

Yours faithfully,
Requester

Subject: Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough-juxta-Penarth

Dear Requester,

Thank you for your emails dated 29 October 2026 regarding Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough-juxta-Penarth.

We have considered the information contained within your email and the additional search terms you have provided.

The Environmental Information Regulations 2004 (EIR) provide a right of access to recorded environmental information held by a public authority. Regulation 2(1) defines environmental information and includes information concerning matters such as the state of the environment, factors affecting the environment, and measures or activities affecting or likely to affect the environment.

Having considered your correspondence, we do not consider that the information you have requested regarding the disconnection, shut off, cap, termination or otherwise interference with the water supply to Great House Farm constitutes a request for environmental information falling within the definition at Regulation 2(1) of the EIR.

The information requested relates to the disconnection of a specific property. The fact that information concerns a water supply to a property does not, of itself, make it “environmental information” for the purposes of regulation 2(1) of the Environmental Information Regulations 2004. The information must fall within one or more of the categories in regulation 2(1). The requested information concerns the fact and circumstances of the property's disconnection. It does not describe the state of any element of the environment, such as water, air, soil or land, within regulation 2(1)(a), nor does it concern a factor such as a substance, energy, noise, radiation, waste, emission, discharge or other release which affects or is likely to affect those elements within regulation 2(1)(b). Further, the disconnection is not a measure or activity affecting or likely to affect environmental elements or factors, or as one designed to protect them, within regulation 2(1)(c). The remaining limbs of regulation 2(1), concerning reports on environmental legislation, relevant economic analyses, and human health and safety or built structures insofar as they are affected by environmental elements, factors, measures or activities, are likewise not engaged.

As the request is directed to the disconnection of this property rather than to any environmental state, effect, factor, measure or activity within regulation 2(1), the information does not fall within the definition of environmental information under the EIR.

Even if this information were considered to be environmental information for the purposes of the Regulations, DCWW would have to refuse the request under Regulation 12(4)(a) as we do not hold the information requested. We do not hold the historical information sought. In accordance with our Retention Policy, any customer or property records from the 1980s that may have existed from that period would fall outside of our data retention periods., and we would no longer hold records dating back to that time. We are also unaware of any other public authority that may hold this information.

For this reason, we are unable to carry out the additional historical searches requested or provide an audit trail identifying search terms and systems in respect of information that is no longer held.

Your email also requested confirmation as to whether any surviving historic records, indexes, work-order records or archived material relating to Great House Farm/Ty Mawr exist. Some such information could constitute environmental information, depending on the nature of the information held and whether it fell within the definition of environmental information in Regulation 2(1). However, for the reasons set out above, we do not hold any historic records, indexes, work-order records or archived material falling within the scope of your request. We are therefore unable to determine whether any such information, if it existed, would constitute environmental information. In any event, as we do not hold the requested information, the request would fall to be refused under Regulation 12(4)(a). We are also unaware of any other public authority that may hold this information.

We hope this clarifies our position.

Thank you
Sumerah

Thank you for your correspondence regarding your request for information under the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) 2000.

Background to your request

We received your original correspondence on 27 June 2026. Since the information requested related to mapping information which is dealt with as part of our routine business, we forwarded your request to our Customer Service Centre (CSC) on 30 June 2026 and confirmed this via our email, also dated 30 June 2026. Regrettably, our CSC team missed the request, and you didn’t receive a response as promised, for which we apologise, once again.

We received your subsequent request for information as a result of the above, on 20 October 2026. I have set out an extract of the correspondence as follows:

Extract of email dated 20 October 2026

“1. Two parts of my email of 27 June asked for recorded information, not for advice. They asked whether Ordnance Survey holds (a) "any map revision notes, resurvey information, or internal documentation explaining changes in naming or label placement for this area between approximately 1950 and 1975", and (b) "any guidance or archival material explaining how estate names or farm names were assigned, repositioned, or reinterpreted across map editions in this period". Please deal with those two parts as a request for information under section 1 of the Freedom of Information Act 2000, or under the Environmental Information Regulations 2004 if you consider the information environmental.

2. For each of (a) and (b), please confirm or deny whether the information is held (section 1(1)(a)). The site is at Llandough-juxta-Penarth, Vale of Glamorgan, within the area of County Series sheet Glamorgan 47 NW, with the map references I gave (38-1-608 and 38-1-334).

3. To make (a) as precise as possible, it covers, for the large-scale (1:2,500 and 1:10,560) plans of this site published between 1950 and 1975: the revision or resurvey dates; any name sheet, name book or field revision record for the names "Ty Mawr", "Great House" or "Great House Farm"; and any record of who supplied or authorised a name or a change to it (for example, an owner, an occupier, a local authority or HM Land Registry), in what capacity, and when.

4. If any of this has been transferred to The National Archives, please give the reference instead of treating that part as not held. I have found that object name books for County Series sheet Glamorgan 47 NW (1898–1942) are at The National Archives as OS 35/2503. Please tell me whether Ordnance Survey holds anything later of the same kind for this area. Thank you for your email of 26 October 2026. I confirm that the site is Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, beside St Dochdwy’s Church at Llandough-juxta-Penarth, Vale of Glamorgan, near Penarth and Cardiff. The relevant mapping area is County Series sheet Glamorgan 47 NW, including map references 38-1-608 and 38-1-334.

Those location and map identifiers should be used as the primary means of identifying the site. The following farm, estate and locality wordings are supporting search terms drawn from different records and periods. They are not all interchangeable names, and their appearance in a source does not by itself establish that they refer to the same building, parcel, estate boundary or title.

Farm and farmhouse nomenclature

Please consider these forms when searching: “Great House Farm”; “Great House Farm, Llandough”; “Great House Farm (GGAT02038s)”; “Great House”; “Great house”; “Greathouse”; “Tŷ Mawr”; “Ty Mawr”; “Ty-mawr”; “Ty Mawr Farm”; “Ty Mawr (Great House)”; “Ty Mawr, Penarth Road, Llandough”; “Cydfin Farm”; “Cydfin Farm or Ty Mawr Farm, (107 a.)”; “Cedfin or Ty Mawr Farm”; “Cedfin”; “Cydwin”; “Cedwyn”; “Cedfyn”; “Cefin”; “Llandough Home Farm”; “Land Doc Home Farm”; “R-W-S-S Farm / Reese’s Farm”; “Llandough Church Farm”; “Church Farm”; “former Great House Farm”; “a 3.4 acre site located adjacent St. Dochdwy Parish Church”; and “LLANDOUGH FARM (Ideal Homes Wales)”. The map form “Ty-mawr” is also recorded on an Ordnance Survey 25-inch map, although the edition and its precise relationship to the site have not been confirmed.

The source status matters. The National Library of Wales Bute catalogue lists “Cydfin Farm or Ty Mawr Farm, (107 a.)” within a 1552 - 1824 catalogue range; that range is not a specific date for the Ty Mawr wording. The 1824 Stewart survey, plan 19, records “Cedfin or Ty Mawr Farm” (Glamorgan Archives DB/E/1). Historical directories use “Great house” and “Greathouse”. The checked 1881 census image reads “Llandough Home Farm”; “Land Doc Home Farm” is a reported competing transcription, and “R-W-S-S Farm / Reese’s Farm” does not appear on that checked page. “Cydwin” and “Cedwyn” are reported research leads whose underlying 16th-century documents have not been verified; “Cedfyn” and “Cefin” are retained as search forms without a confirmed primary occurrence. “Llandough Church Farm” and “Church Farm” are source-specific terms whose connection to this site is not established by the cited records. The 1994 Ideal Homes Wales plan uses “LLANDOUGH FARM” for this development site, while other records use Llandough Farm for a separate farmstead; please distinguish records by their mapped location rather than by that wording alone.

Other indexed phrases, including “an 800-year-old house”, “the ten-roomed house”, “ancient Welsh house” and “the farm / the whole of the farm”, are descriptions rather than established property names.
